messages:
maria: quick heads-up — int4 bring-up for sparsepathway-v2 shows a ~6% exact-match drop on our golden prompts vs float16. Did we change any dedupe or sampling before this rollout?

sam: which golden file/version are you running against? i can repro locally if you share run id.

maria: golden/2026-03/sparsepathway/goldset_v3.jsonl. run id qbench-171125, quant seed=42. core stats: exact_match 0.881 -> 0.827, accept_rate 0.93 -> 0.888. snippet: 
```
run: qbench-171125
model: sparsepathway-v2-int4
metric: exact_match 0.881 -> 0.827
failed: 186/3000 prompts (top issues: truncation, split-tokens)
```

taylor: ok quick triage plan: 1) reproduce float16 on same goldset (rule out data change) 2) run dedupe with stricter threshold (0.92) and compare fail overlap 3) surface top-100 failing prompts for manual relabel / edgecase tagging. can we do (1) now?

sam: running float16 now. fyi earlier qbench merge bumped dedupe default to 0.9 -> could increase near-dup retention. command I used for dedupe: 
```
python -m curation.dedupe --input goldset_v3.jsonl --thresh 0.90 --out goldset_v3.dedup.jsonl
```
if that changed, we might have introduced paraphrase collisions into the goldset.

lee: labeling capacity: can take 200 flagged prompts by EOD if we push a slice to the label queue. otherwise ~500 by tomorrow midday.

dev-bot: [qbench-ci] pipeline qbench-171125 completed with status FAILED (regression detected). See: https://ci.internal/qbench/171125/logs

maria: thanks. I'll run stricter dedupe (0.92) and rerun int4 bench. will also generate a failing-prompts export: failures/qbench-171125-fails.jsonl and tag by failure-type.

sam: note about tokenizer: int4 kernel uses tokenizer-v2 byte-offset changes — tokenization diffs can create perceived hallucinations. please regen tokenization with tokenizer:v2 before comparing. command: 
```
python -m curation.tokenize --model sparsepathway-v2 --tokenizer v2 --input goldset_v3.dedup.jsonl --out gold_tok.jsonl
```

taylor: if dedupe+tokenizer fixes don't explain it, we should snapshot the top-200 fails and run a small human audit (gold relabel) + a rollback plan: pin dedicated canary to gold_v2 for 24h. I can coordinate rollout with infra.

maria: agreed. i'll: 
- run dedupe @0.92 and regen tokenization (now)
- rerun qbench-int4 locally (strict-seed)
- upload failures and tag for labeling
- open a canary rollback PR to pin to gold_v2 on dedicated (10% traffic)

sam: ack. if you want speedup, use --sample 3000 and --parallel 8 on qbench. also check kv-cache shortprefix behavior — we saw similar regressions when kv-truncation changed.

lee: once the fail export is live, ping me and i'll drop the top 200 into the expedited label queue. i'll mark them with label: "int4-triage" so we can track.

maria: exported failures at s3://redwood-curation/exports/qbench-171125-fails.jsonl (tagged by failure_type). dedupe run used thresh=0.92. rerunning qbench now.

dev-bot: [deploy-bot] canary rollback PR opened: #4826 pin goldset->gold_v2 (10% canary) by maria. CI: pending.

sam: ran float16 reproduction on gold_v3.dedup.jsonl with tokenizer v2 — float16 matches baseline (exact_match 0.880 -> 0.879). so data change alone doesn't explain drop. suggests quant path or kernel/tokenizer interaction.

taylor: good repro info. next steps: 1) reproduce int4 with exact same tokenized inputs on host that will run production kernel 2) run binary bisect: int8->int4 and kernel versions to narrow change 3) schedule 1-hour label audit for top-50 edgecases. tagging owners: @lee for labels, @sam for kernel bisect, @maria for canary.

maria: putting owners in calendar for a quick sync in 30min. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: leaving a short note in the dataset changelog: "dedupe threshold bumped to 0.92 for triage run; tokenization regenerated with tokenizer-v2; monitoring added for kv-cache shortprefix"

lee: noted. will update label tracker once items in queue.

maria: i'll follow up with postmortem if we find a root cause. for now rolling canary to 10% hold.

taylor: thanks — keep the thread updated.
